transcript.full_text: This is how you turn Claude into a social media machine. Most people don't know this, but you can just type /analyze into Claude, paste any video link and get a full analysis. The transcript, format, topic, angle, storytelling structure, hook analysis, visual layout, all the information you'd want. And you can do this for dozens of videos at a time. So as I scroll social media, I copy the video URLs for anything interesting I see and then paste them all into Claude in one shot. But here's the cool part. Not only do I get the individual video breakdowns, but I can also batch analyze that entire set of videos at once. And this gives me the hidden trends, insights and patterns that I just would not have seen otherwise. Now to enable this, all you have to do is set up the Sandcastles.ai plugin inside of Claude. Once you have it, it'll give you access to 14 different social media Claude skills, including /analyze. This plugin is what I personally use to run all of my content research, and it's how I've been able to grow so much faster. It's kind of like giving a social media power up to your version of Claude. If you want me to send through a video on how to set all this up so you can access those social media skills, comment "Claude" and I'll send it through.

payoff_alignment.reasoning: The mechanism is real and shown working on screen, so the promise is substantively delivered. It drops to a 3 because the payoff depends on installing a specific third-party plugin that the hook does not mention — the viewer is sold 'turn Claude into X' and finds at 0:38 that the answer is 'buy this add-on'. Delivered, but with a disclosure deferred to the second half.

what_to_steal: Name the exact command or UI action in the first ten seconds ('/analyze'), not the benefit. A literal string the viewer can type is more persuasive than any adjective.
Show the tool working before naming the product. The demo runs 0:03-0:37; the product is named at 0:38, once the capability is already believed.
Escalate scope at the midpoint: one video, then dozens at once. The second, larger claim lands only because the first was demonstrated.

Enumerate the output fields aloud ('transcript, format, topic, angle, storytelling structure, hook analysis, visual layout'). A list of concrete deliverables does the work a vague 'full breakdown' cannot.
Split layout keeps a face on screen while the screen recording carries the information — retains talking-head connection without giving up demo space.
what_not_to_steal: The 13K-to-20.1K follower overlay: it is unverifiable, undated, and only persuasive coming from an account whose numbers the viewer can check.
'Changed social media forever' framing, which depends on the tool being genuinely new at time of posting and ages badly.
Deferring the paid dependency to 0:38. It converts, but it is the reason hook alignment scores 3 rather than 5, and it costs trust on rewatch.

confidence.notes: Duration (63s) and cut count (~22, giving 21 cuts/min) reported by the vision tool, not frame-counted. WPM computed from the transcript via scripts/metrics.py. Views, likes and comments are null because the Instagram watch tool exposes no engagement data — the two follower figures are claims made inside the video, not measurements. Section boundaries are inferred from speech beats and rounded to the second.
